newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's CDC bank raises Q1 growth outlook.
newsitem.headline: France's CDC bank raises Q1 growth outlook.

text.p: French state bank Caisse des Depot et Consignations (CDC) on Monday raised its estimate for French economic growth in the first quarter to 0.6 percent and said it expected the same pace of growth in the second quarter.
The first quarter estimate was raised from 0.4 percent previously. CDC left its fourth quarter 1996 estimate unchanged at 0.2 percent.
CDC said the estimates were based on a synthetic leading indicator and were not a forecast.

CDC said in a statement, "In 1997 Q1, the weakness of real activity data plays a smoother role and is compensated for by a better performance of the stock markets, interest rates (particularly French) alongside an improving external environment."
CDC also released figures for the first time translating the predictions of its leading indicator into figures in line with official GDP figures released by national statistics institute INSEE.
Both the INSEE figures and the CDC leading indicator are adjusted for seasonal variations but the CDC estimate also adjusts for the number of working days in the period whereas INSEE does not.
It said a reduced number of working days in the first quarter meant the its 0.6 quarter-on-quarter growth estimate was equivalent to a 0.2 percent rise in the INSEE data.

However, the number of working days in the second quarter meant its 0.6 percent rise would translate into an increase of 1.4 percent from the first quarter if the INSEE method of calculation were used.
